Jordan F.: Working on a compact Dedicated Capacity cheatsheet for fast onboarding. Goal: one-page Quick Commands, one-page Migration Checklist, and a tiny Go SDK example. Will also sweep for broken handbook anchors. Quick thoughts?
Mina C.: Love it. Make the Quick Commands truly copy/pasteable: terraform + python + go. Call out the exact terraform var names (`reserved_pool_replicas` vs `replicas`) and a clear pre-provision quota check.
Luis G.: For Migration Checklist, include a minimal smoke test step (50rps for 2m) and a short rollback recipe (drain, scale to 0, revert infra, re-enable). Keep it checklist style.
docs-bot: link-check: found broken anchor in handbook/dedicated/operations.md -> '#preemption-behaviour' not present. Also detected redirect /handbook/dedicated/old-sla -> /handbook/dedicated/sla-and-slos (301).
Jordan F.: Thanks bot. I'll point SLA links to /handbook/dedicated/sla-and-slos and add a TODO for anchor cleanup. I'll also add a note: "SLA numbers live on the SLA page; do not hardcode percentiles in Quickstart."
Mina C.: For Go example, show ScalePolicy with cooldown_seconds and an explicit quota check comment. Example should be minimal but compile-ish.
Jordan F.: Draft Go snippet (will include in Quick Commands):
```go
package main

import (
  "os"
  "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk"
)

func main() {
  // ensure quota check via management API before calling Create
  client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  policy := redwood.ScalePolicy{Type: "autoscale", CooldownSeconds: 300}
  _, err := client.CreateDedicatedCapacity(redwood.DedicatedCapacity{
    Name:    "prod-reserved",
    GPUType: "a100",
    Replicas: 3,
    ScalePolicy: policy,
    Isolation: "reserved-pool",
  })
  if err != nil {
    panic(err)
  }
}
```
Luis G.: Nice. For Terraform snippet, show the quota data block and use `reserved_pool_replicas`:
```terraform
data "redwood_quota" "current" {}
resource "redwood_dedicated_capacity" "prod" {
  name                   = "prod-reserved"
  gpu_type               = "a100"
  reserved_pool_replicas = 3
  scale_policy           = "autoscale"
  isolation              = "reserved-pool"
}
```
Mina C.: Python snippet too, with cooldown shown explicitly:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
client.create_dedicated_capacity(
  name="prod-reserved",
  gpu_type="a100",
  replicas=3,
  scale_policy={"type":"autoscale","cooldown_seconds":300},
  isolation="reserved-pool"
)
```
QA-bot: checklist-scan: recommend adding post-provision smoke test step: run 50rps synthetic load for 2 minutes and assert no more than X% error rate (team to define X in QA plan). Also include monitoring alert for 24h.
Jordan F.: Adding smoke test and monitor step to checklist. Migration Checklist (short): 1) export routing config, 2) provision in staging, 3) run smoke test (50rps, 2m), 4) rotate automation keys, 5) lift traffic in 10% increments with 30m observation windows, 6) monitor for 24h.
Luis G.: Include a small "Runtime notes" box: default cooldown=300s, preemption semantics differ between isolation modes (reserved-pool = stronger isolation, tenant = possible preemption). Link runtime ticket #451 for current behaviour.
Jordan F.: Will do. Also adding brief guidance on wording: "Do not publish percentile SLAs in how-to docs; link to the SLA page instead."
Mina C.: One small accessibility nit: use consistent casing for config keys (snake_case) across snippets.
Jordan F.: Good catch. I'll standardize. I'll open a draft PR and tag #eng-runtime, #docs-review, and #qa. PR will include an anchors TODO so we can coordinate link fixes with the handbook team.
